**Please note that Wood Mackenzie will be launching our full Metals & Mining Corporate Tool in October 2012. If you have any further questions please contact –** **sheona.griffiths@woodmac.com** # Capital investment to peak in 2014 Capital investment in metals and mining operations across the globe will increase in 2014, to a peak of US$151.8 billion. Initial findings from Wood Mackenzie’s Metals & Mining Corporate Tool, which includes over 4,100 assets, 1,200 companies across 94 regimes, suggests the investment boom will continue into next year and beyond for copper, lead, aluminium, and zinc. US$521 billion investment is forecast over the next four years, a 22% increase in spend compared to 2009-2012. Not all commodities will see investment growth. Peak investment in copper is forecast in 2015, at US$42 billion. Whilst investment in the coal industry is expected to be US$42billion in 2012, declining thereafter. Capital investment in iron ore will continue to increase until 2014 when US$37.2 billion will be spent, predominantly on expansion projects in Brazil coming on line. China, Australia and Canada will attract most of this new capital investment between 2013-2016, despite investment in China and Australia declining by 29% and 6% respectively year on year over the same timeframe. For the next four years capital investment will increasingly be focused on Chile and Peru, as a result of the major copper projects coming online – most notably Caserones (150kt/a), Ministro Mina Hales (200kt/a), Las Bambas (400kt/a) and Sierra Gorda (250kt/a). Capital investment to peak in 2014 ## Expansion capital spend by commodity Over the last few years, on the back of high commodity prices, there have been unprecedented levels of projects proposed across the metals and mining industry. It is only since commodity prices bounced back from the financial crisis of 2008 and confidence returned to the banking sector, that mining companies have had sufficient confidence and access to capital to commit enough investment to significantly increase global production. Expansion capital (including both greenfield and brownfield projects) expenditure across the metals and mining industry is set to peak in 2014 at US$151.8 billion. In 2014 over 70% of capital investment will be in copper, coal, and iron ore. The timing of this global spend of investment varies slightly by commodity, with copper projects steadily increasing until 2015 when expansion capital will exceed three times of that invested in 2009 - a time when many projects were delayed during the global financial crisis. Global coal investment will peak this year at US$42 billion and iron ore in 2014 at US$37.2billion respectively. With coal and iron ore prices declining, and costs having steadily increased during this time, the forecast margins on these projects are narrowing resulting in many projects being

reviewed and in some cases, delayed. There continues to be steady growth in copper project development, with investment peaking in 2015 at US$42.3Bn. However due to the significant ‘barriers to entry’ to copper mining and the many obstacles facing project developers, it is unlikely that a significant long-term surplus of mined and hence refined copper will build up in the foreseeable future, despite the continuing surge in project development activity. Given the three to four year time frame for bringing new mining projects into production, decisions made over the next twelve months will influence the supply picture for copper in the period immediately beyond 2016. If mining companies are discouraged from developing projects by the present uncertain economic climate or the apparent wealth of projects already in construction, then a deficit in mined copper could return in the latter half of this decade. ### **Timeline of peak capital spend** |**2010**|**2012**|**2013**|**2014**|**2015**| |---|---|---|---|---| |**Alumina**

0 Capital investment to peak in 2014 ## Expansion capital spend by country China continues to dominate the metals and mining industry, with almost a third of the global expansion capital being invested in predominantly coal projects through domestic Chinese coal companies. However investment in China’s metals and mining industry peaked in 2009 at US$45.2bn and will steadily decline by 22% yoy over the next four years. By 2016 the top ten countries for metals and mining investment will have varied considerably. In 2016, Canada will be the most attractive country for metals and mining investment with over US$11bn being invested in projects. This investment in Canada will be predominantly in copper (US$6.7bn), gold (US$1.7bn bn), and zinc (US$1.4bn). However investment in the Canadian coal industry will increase by more than eleven times the investment in 2009, peaking at US$803m in 2016. Chinese coal investment is to supply the domestic market, predominantly in the provinces of Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia and Shanxi. In Xinjiang these projects are to supply the power stations to power the growing aluminium smelter projects, which have a combined ultimate capacity of 13.6Mt. Inner Mongolia and Shanxi are China's two largest coal producing provinces and contain almost half of China's coal reserves. Projects in these provinces will be crucial for meeting China's projected coal demand growth. ### **Expansion capital spend by country** 160

Metals and Mining Corporate Tool Insight - September 2012 Page 6 of 10 Capital investment to peak in 2014 ## Expansion capital spend by company Metals and mining project developers are facing considerable challenges such as escalating capital an

d operating costs, the shortage of skilled labour, stricter permitting regulations, increased opposition to mining projects from local communities, unpredictable fiscal policies and uncertain security of tenure in some countries. However, this is not deterring the major mining companies from continuing to develop both greenfield and brownfield projects across the metals and mining industry, albeit at a decreasing rate. The combined capital spend of the major mining companies is forecast to be US$34.3bn in 2016. Vale’s capital investment is predominantly focused on their iron ore projects in Brazil, and Voisey’s Bay nickel project in Canada. ### **Expansion capital spend by company** 160

## Conclusion Despite several companies announcing project delays in the metals and mining industry, our analysis of over 4,000 assets shows that capital investment in the industry will peak in 2014 with US$151.8 billion dollars being spent globally. Most of the investment in 2014 will be focused on the copper industry (accounting for US$42 billion), closely followed by the capital investment in the domestic Chinese coal industry accounting for US$28.6billion. Over the next four years, Canada will emerge as the most attractive country for investment - particularly for Greenfield polymetallic mines. Capital investment in China will decrease as their coal projects come online, particularly in the Shanxi East and Xinjiang provinces to supply the aluminium and steel industries respectively. Previously untapped resources in developing countries are also attracting capital investment. Like Chile and Peru before them, the Philippines, Pakistan, Ecuador, and Mozambique will attract Metals and mining capital investment over the next four years. Metals and Mining
